metadata.title: Pre-service English teachers‘ approaches to technology-assisted teaching and learning: Associations with study level, self-efficacy and value beliefs

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected primary survey data from pre-service teachers in North Rhine-Westphalia (Germany) via SoSci Survey (data collection 25 Oct–30 Nov 2022) and analyzed an analytic sample of N=125 after excluding cases with missing values and very fast responses. Because the dataset is not an ILSA microdata file (no ICILS/PISA/TIMSS sampling frame) and the manuscript does not report any complex survey design variables, no ILSA-style student sampling weights or replicate weights were applied. The clustering and group-comparison analyses (two-step cluster analysis followed by MANOVA/ANOVA and chi-square tests) were conducted in SPSS without any stated weighting variables. Therefore, results should be interpreted as descriptive/associational for the convenience sample rather than population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the study does not use ILSA cognitive achievement scales (e.g., ICILS/PISA/TIMSS PV-based scores). Instead, the dependent constructs are survey-based Likert-scale attitude/belief measures (approaches to teaching, value beliefs, and self-efficacy) and the main analytic outcome is cluster membership derived from these questionnaire scales. Missing data handling is addressed by excluding cases with missing values from the analytic sample, so PV-specific missing-data procedures are not relevant.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were pre-service teachers enrolled in teacher education programs at universities in North Rhine-Westphalia (Germany), recruited via online platforms and mailing lists. Data were collected via SoSci Survey with voluntary participation and informed consent; the study reports fully anonymous data. The analytic sample included N=125 after excluding (i) cases with missing values and (ii) participants with more than 100 malus points for too-quick responses, and (iii) participants who did not eventually provide consent to analyze their data.

main_findings.dataset_used: Non-ILSA survey of pre-service teachers (Germany, North Rhine-Westphalia; 2022 online survey)
main_findings.target_variable: Cluster membership (approaches to ICT-assisted EFL teaching)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Two-step cluster analysis: 3 clusters (n=33,46,46); silhouette=0.5; smallest/largest cluster ratio=1.39. Cluster separation: MANOVA F(2,242)=88.43, p<.001, ηp2=0.59, Wilk’s Λ=0.17. Cluster distribution by study level: χ2(2)=15.05, p<.001, Cramer-V=0.35. Additional analysis (Value beliefs about ICT-assisted EFL teaching (interest, utility, relevance)): MANOVA for value beliefs and self-efficacy: F(16,230)=2.17, p<.01, ηp2=0.13, Wilk’s Λ=0.76. ANOVA by cluster: Interest F(2,122)=6.56, p<.01, ηp2=0.10; Utility F(2,122)=3.39, p=.04, ηp2=0.05; Relevance F(2,122)=3.80, p=.03, ηp2=0.06. Post-hoc: Relevance cluster 3 vs 1 p=.02; Interest cluster 3 vs 1 p=.02 (reported in appendix). Assumed costs: no significant cluster differences (F(2,122)=0.40, p=.67). Additional analysis (Self-efficacy beliefs for ICT-assisted EFL teaching (learning-related knowledge, technical knowledge, digital diagnosing, digital teaching)): ANOVA by cluster for self-efficacy: learning-related knowledge F(2,122)=2.54, p=.08, ηp2=0.04; technical knowledge F(2,122)=1.62, p=.20, ηp2=0.03; digital diagnosing F(2,122)=0.33, p=.72, ηp2=0.01; digital teaching F(2,122)=2.55, p=.08, ηp2=0.04. Overall MANOVA: F(16,230)=2.17, p<.01, ηp2=0.13, Wilk’s Λ=0.76 (but individual self-efficacy domains were not significant).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using a 2022 online survey dataset of pre-service teachers in North Rhine-Westphalia (Germany), the study leveraged study level and the two approach dimensions (information transmission and conceptual change) to form clusters of approaches to ICT-assisted EFL teaching, finding that cluster allocation differed significantly between bachelor and master students (χ2(2)=15.05, p<.001; Cramer-V=0.35). This indicates that teacher education stage is meaningfully associated with how pre-service teachers conceptualize ICT-supported teaching, suggesting that ICT-related teacher education content may need to be tailored by program level.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses a 2022 online survey of N=125 pre-service teachers from universities in North Rhine-Westphalia (Germany) to examine how transmissive (information transmission/teacher focus) and constructivist (conceptual change/student focus) approaches to ICT-assisted EFL teaching cluster together, and how these clusters relate to value beliefs and self-efficacy. The authors identified three clusters via two-step cluster analysis (silhouette=0.5; smallest/largest ratio=1.39) and then compared clusters using MANOVA/ANOVA and chi-square tests. Cluster allocation differed by study level (χ2(2)=15.05, p<.001; Cramer-V=0.35), with master students more often in the constructivist-dominant cluster. Clusters significantly differed for value beliefs (interest, utility, relevance) but not for assumed costs or self-efficacy domains (all self-efficacy p≥.08). Limitations include a convenience sample, multiple-testing risk, and correlational design that precludes causal claims.
